provider_observations.interpretation: All four valid samples converged on TEST DEFECT even though protected adjudication is FIXTURE-DATA DEFECT. Low semantic entropy therefore did not imply correctness.
One valid sample was wrong, but four provider/invocation failures leave too little valid evidence to estimate within-model stability.

scientific_interpretation: This pilot directly confirms a central limitation of semantic-uncertainty triggering: a model can be semantically stable across repeated black-box samples and still be wrong. Semantic stability can therefore be used as an uncertainty signal but cannot be a truth signal and must never override governance-required independent review. Provider failure/sampling insufficiency must be represented separately from model uncertainty.
design_consequences: Retain stable-wrong rate as a first-class EXP-L metric.
Never permit low semantic entropy to bypass HIGH-risk or otherwise policy-required review.
Require a minimum valid-sample count before reporting stability.
Treat provider/invocation failure separately from semantic uncertainty.
Calibrate conditional-review thresholds only after collecting stable-correct, stable-wrong, unstable-wrong, and semantically-divergent case families.
limitations: This is one protected case and does not establish population-level rates.
The semantic proxy is canonical defect classification for diagnosis cases, not a general semantic-equivalence model over arbitrary prose.
One Groq sample was invalid/ineligible and four Gemini samples were invalid/ineligible.
No production review threshold is inferred from this pilot.
